answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens into an audit pool where each identity acts as an ember of verification. A game-theoretic multi-agent auditing protocol selects random validators to audit transactions, slashing stakes for fraudulent attestations. Network trust graphs are analyzed via topological cut verifications, treating every agent as a vertex. If malicious actors create fake identities, boundary cuts isolate them, making total attacker cost superlinear relative to swarm size as honest nodes illuminate collusion like a lantern.
